title: Centrally concentrated molecular gas driving galactic-scale ionized gas outflows in star-forming galaxies
question: Why do some main-sequence star-forming galaxies reach the star-formation rate surface density threshold to launch large-scale ionised gas winds while other similar galaxies matched in inclination, mass, and total SFR do not?

data.sensitivity: 0.8 M_sun pc^-2 molecular gas mass surface density

what.value: xCOLD GASS survey catalogue used to construct the global control sample

evidence.quote: In Section 3.1, we use a control sample derived solely from xCOLD GASS (referred to as the “xCOLD GASS controls”) for the interpretation of the global/integrated results (i.e. we do not include the original, viable ALMA controls).

what.value: GAMA DR2/DR3 catalogue global properties, spectroscopic redshifts, MAGPHYS M_* and SFR, and SersicCatAllv07 ellipticities

evidence.quote: We extract additional global properties for our objects (e.g. $NUV-r$) from the Galaxy And Mass Assembly (GAMA) DR2/DR3 catalogue (cite: liske15; baldry18) with their respective uncertainties to supplement the interpretation of our results.
Spaxel areas $\rm A_{\rm spaxel}$ are corrected for inclination ($i$) using the GAMA survey ellipticity values from SersicCatAllv07 (cite: kelvin12), such that the spaxel areas equate to:

From the sample of 15 edge-on SAMI Galaxy Survey galaxies identified by (cite: ho16) as having large-scale winds, we select the 11 objects with $\log (\rm M_{*} /M_{\odot}) > 9.2$ in order to avoid low metallicity objects, where $\rm \upalpha_{CO}$ (i.e. the CO-$\rm H_2$ conversion function) could be large.

recipe.goal: Clean ALMA data cubes and extract global CO(1-0) spectra
recipe.method: Clean dirty cubes interactively over ~50 channels centred on peak CO(1-0) emission using tclean. Smooth trimmed cubes spatially with a 2D Gaussian kernel (sigma_smooth = 1.5 spaxels), collapse spectrally, threshold at >1 sigma within an ~200x200 spaxel spatial region to build a spatial aperture mask, apply to original trimmed cube, and collapse spatially to extract integrated spectra.
key_parameters: ~50 channels centred on peak of CO(1) emission
mask threshold > 1 sigma within ~200 x 200 spaxels
assumptions: Systemic velocity defined from GAMA spectroscopic redshift

recipe.goal: Measure integrated CO(1-0) fluxes, luminosities, and global molecular gas masses and compare with xCOLD GASS controls
recipe.method: Numerically integrate global ALMA CO(1-0) profiles over channels with signal >3 sigma of line-free noise. Convert S_CO to L_CO following Solomon et al. (1997) and multiply by variable alpha_CO from Accurso et al. (2017). Compare global gas fraction and SFE with matched xCOLD GASS control pairs using swing plots.
key_parameters: signal detection threshold > 3 sigma; 300 km s^-1 velocity range for non-detections (S/N < 3)
xCOLD GASS control matching: 0.3 dex box in SFR and M_*, i > 50 deg, non-AGN, random 80% subsampling
assumptions: Standard LambdaCDM cosmology with H_0 = 70 km s^-1 Mpc^-1, Omega_m0 = 0.3, Omega_Lambda = 0.7 and Chabrier (2003) IMF
Variable alpha_CO from Accurso et al. (2017) using Pettini & Pagel (2004) metallicity calibration from 3'' SAMI apertures and MAGPHYS M_* and SFR

recipe.goal: Construct CO(1-0) moment maps (zeroth, first, second) and position-velocity diagrams
recipe.method: Smooth cubes spectrally by a factor of 4 and spatially by a factor of 1.5 with a 2D Gaussian kernel, mask values below 3 sigma of the smoothed noise in the unsmoothed cube over a ~22''x22'' box and ~45-50 channels, and collapse along spectral axis to get Moment 0, 1, and 2 maps. Rotate cube by SAMI position angle and collapse perpendicular to disk across a slit containing 95% of CO(1) emission to make PVDs.
key_parameters: spatial box ~22'' x 22'', channel range ~45 - 50 channels
spectral smoothing factor = 4, spatial smoothing factor = 1.5, mask threshold = 3 sigma
PVD slit width enclosing 95% of CO(1) emission (e.g. 1.6'', 2.4'', 2.0'' for GAMA593680, GAMA106389, GAMA417678)
assumptions: Position angle taken from SAMI Galaxy Survey catalogues

recipe.goal: Compute spatially resolved surface density maps and radial profiles of SFR, molecular gas, SFE, and gas fraction
recipe.method: Create SAMI SFR maps from BPT star-forming masked, extinction-corrected H-alpha maps. Degrade ALMA Moment 0 maps to SAMI PSF resolution via 2D Gaussian convolution and re-bin both ALMA and SAMI maps to SAMI PSF scale (~1 kpc) using 25 grid offsets (5 in RA x 5 in Dec). Correct spaxel areas for inclination, divide maps to form SFE and f_MH2, and bin spaxels by value and by galactocentric radius normalised by r_eff.
key_parameters: 25 re-binning grid offsets (5 in RA x 5 in Dec, 0 - 0.8 x bin size) to scale spaxels to sigma_PSF (~2'', ~1 kpc)
SAMI control selection boxes: 0.6 x 0.7 dex in SFR-M_* around low-M_* (<10) and high-M_* (>10) outflow-types
assumptions: Leroy et al. (2013) relation used to convert Sigma_SFR into Sigma_CO,H2 for SAMI controls
Inclination correction factor 1/cos(i) from GAMA SersicCatAllv07 ellipticity

score_reason: Raw ALMA, SAMI, GAMA, and xCOLD GASS datasets are public and the mathematical equations for flux, luminosity, moment maps, beam degradation, and re-binning are explicitly written out, but key tclean parameters, interactive masks, and custom analysis scripts are not released, and the ALMA project code in the text is a template placeholder.
rediscovery_reason: The ALMA data (2017.1.00601.S) and SAMI/GAMA catalogs are public, and Table 2 provides exact per-galaxy integrated CO(1-0) fluxes, linewidths, redshifts, luminosities, and gas fractions for all 16 galaxies that serve as a quantitative benchmark.
